analysis:
Documentation-only PR touching docs/provider/direct-mode.md and docs/provider/two-mac-cluster.md. No source, key-handling, or protocol code changed, so nothing alters the threat-model controls directly. Review of the documented behavior:

(1) direct-mode.md: adds a KV slot grant / HTTP 503 reslice note (line 56-59). This is an availability description (T-016/T-029 neighborhood) and weakens no auth or encryption control. The local endpoint auth description (LocalAuthResponder, 0600 token, loopback default, no TLS) is unchanged.

(2) two-mac-cluster.md: documents that Qwen3.8 27B TP speculative assistant decoding is used only on `darkbloom cluster local` or with `mtp_mode=on`. In the `on` case the pair is documented as not offered to the coordinator ('not offered for public traffic'). This is consistent with the T-007/TB-002 posture of not exposing unqualified modes to public traffic. Whether the code actually enforces the exclusion from coordinator registration is an unverified contract, since no code is supplied. Also documented: constrained_decoding_unsupported HTTP 400 refusal on Qwen pairs, with coordinator failover to a single Mac in a separate platform branch. That coordinator behavior is platform-owned and unverified here. The retry/backoff rule for coordinator-paired parts (60 minutes or a later approval) is described. The manual update section states pairs have no auto-update, so updates depend on operator action. That is a pre-existing availability and version-currency consideration (T-043 region), not a regression.

Remaining integration questions: whether the implementation really keeps the assistant out of coordinator registration under `mtp_mode=on`, and whether stale worker versions on a pair are gated by approval digests (build-pinned approvals are noted). No concrete security regression is visible in the supplied docs.
